title: The Smell That Fixed London in 18 Days #history #shorts
description:
In the summer of 1858 the River Thames smelled so bad that Parliament soaked its own curtains in bleach. Then it did in 18 days what it had refused to do for years.

Facts used: Nearly three million Londoners' sewage ran into the Thames. Michael Faraday wrote to The Times in 1855 after dropping white cards into the river and watching them vanish. In the heat of June 1858 the curtains of Parliament were soaked in chloride of lime. Benjamin Disraeli, the Chancellor of the Exchequer, fled a committee room with his papers in one hand and a handkerchief over his nose. Moving Parliament's business to Oxford or St Albans was considered. Disraeli's bill passed in 18 days, and Joseph Bazalgette's sewers, finished in 1875, still carry London's sewage.

The clerk's exchange is a dramatisation.
